sentences.text: Tornieria is a genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur found in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
This animal is characterized by having robust hind legs and short tibiae.
According to Gregory S. Paul, Tornieria was 25 meters long and weighed 10 metric tons.
A maximum known femur length of 138 centimeters suggests Tornieria reached 26 meters in length and 23 tons in weight.
A 2026 study found evidence of at least five independent origins or reversals of pneumaticity in anterior caudal vertebrae among neosauropods, including Tornieria africana.
German paleontologist Eberhard Fraas discovered two sauropod specimens at Quarry A in the Tendaguru Beds in 1907.
Eberhard Fraas originally named the species Gigantosaurus africanus and G. robustus in 1908.
Richard Sternfeld renamed the genus Tornieria in 1911 to honor the German herpetologist Gustav Tornier.
Richard Sternfeld proposed the name Tornieria in 1911 for two species, T. robusta and T. africana.
Werner Janensch re-evaluated Tornieria in 1922, concluding that T. africana was actually Barosaurus africanus.
In 1961, Werner Janensch suggested T. africana was an African variety of Barosaurus and T. robusta belonged to a macronarian later named Janenschia by Wild in 1991.
Kristian Remes concluded in 2006 that Tornieria is a distinct and valid genus separate from Barosaurus.
Remes (2006) concluded that Tornieria is a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae.
The genus Tornieria was established by Sternfeld in 1911.
The species T. africana was originally described by Fraas in 1908.
Tornieria is currently considered a distinct genus from Barosaurus with two species, T. africana and T. gracilis.
A 2006 cladistic analysis concluded that Tornieria is the sister taxon to a clade formed by Barosaurus and Diplodocus.
Tornieria is classified as a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae.
Tornieria lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
There are 7 recorded fossil occurrences of Tornieria in the Paleobiology Database.
